chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his brother al-Hasan, from Zura'ah ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said: I heard him saying:
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, promised two punishments for the wealth of the orphan. As for one of them, it is the punishment of the Hereafter, which is the Fire.
And as for the punishment of this world, it is His saying, the Mighty and Majestic:
And let those fear who, should they leave behind them weakly offspring, would fear on their account, so let them be careful of (their duty to) Allah, and let them speak right words.
He means by that: Let him fear that he will be left behind in his offspring, just as he dealt with these orphans.
ai.seo_question: What are the two punishments promised for usurping the wealth of orphans?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to highlight the dual nature of divine retribution for misappropriating orphan wealth, linking the eternal penalty of Hellfire with a tangible worldly consequence. The scholar interprets the Quranic command for patriarchs to fear for their weak offspring as a reciprocal principle: the manner in which one cares for orphans sets the precedent for how one's own descendants will be treated, emphasizing social justice and familial continuity.
